title: Those Who Discuss before the Sages
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: The designation applied to Shimon ben Azai, Shimon ben Zoma [as printed; the supplied text reads ben Zuta], Chanan the Egyptian and Chananyah ben Chachinai. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak also includes Shimon the Timnite, as set out in [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.4) [Hyman cites 17a]. [Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.2.4.3) lists Ben Azai and Ben Zoma as “those who discuss before the sages” and separately lists Chanina ben Chachinai and R’ Elazar ben Matya as “students.”[^4]

notes.text: The supplied Sanhedrin locator is17a; the complete rank list is at17b and reads ben Zoma where the notice’s first list has ben Zuta. The later Jerusalem Talmud list separates discussants from students, rather than calling the latter the former’s pupils. Timnite is not Yemenite.

No new primary scalar was supplied for this entry. The earlier complete Sanhedrin 17b rank-list consultation is inherited alongside supplied יז. (17a), including ben Zoma beside the first supplied ben Zuta. Neither the first list nor its Chanan/Chananyah forms is silently harmonized with the later Jerusalem Talmud list. Students names a separate category, not the preceding discussants' pupils. Timnite is not Yemenite. The conventional Nachman bar Yitzchak expansion is retained as inherited, while the uninspected Jerusalem Talmud Elazar title remains R'; no authority merge follows.

Hyman’s printed first list has ben Zoma, which agrees with Sanhedrin 17b. The supplied Hebrew keeps ben Zuta. The Bavli gives Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak’s five-name form, and Rashi identifies the third Shimon as Shimon the Timnite. The Yerushalmi distinguishes discussants from students. The consulted Hebrew version names the student Chananyah ben Chachinai and spells out Rabbi Elazar ben Matya, while Hyman’s notice gives Chanina and abbreviates Elazar’s title and name.

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sanhedrin.17b.4.2) explains that Rav Nachman adds Shimon the Timnite to the four and describes how the five sat before the elders. [Heilprin’s entry on the group](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=942&lang=en) sets the Bavli and Yerushalmi lists side by side.
